thread:
Priya R: FYI OrchardRx POC hit a showstopper. Their web client (using fetch + ReadableStream) intermittently receives truncated JSON and Chrome logs `ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING`. Demo tomorrow morning. Need a quick triage. cc @Noah B @Jordan M

Noah B: annoying. do we have request id / sample response? are they using any proxy in front of the app?

Priya R: request_id=orx-poc-20260324-a1. They are hitting our hosted endpoint directly (no customer-managed proxy) from their VPC-restricted office wifi. They sent a captured response chunk file: first bytes look like `data: {"event": "msg", "body": "Payment token: \uD83D` then next chunk starts `\uDE0A"}`

Jordan M: that is a surrogate pair split mid-sequence (high surrogate 0xD83D then low surrogate 0xDE0A). If the chunk boundary splits a UTF-16/UTF-8 multibyte glyph, the TextDecoder or JSON.parse will error. Two angles: client-side accumulate & decode with streaming-safe TextDecoder, or server/runtime avoid splitting inside UTF-8 codepoint.

SupportBot: Log bundle uploaded for orx-poc-20260324-a1: https://s3.redwood/logs/orx-poc-20260324-a1.tar.gz :file_cabinet:

Noah B: check runtime logs for any `upstream timeout` or gzip flush. Also look for `Content-Encoding: gzip` or `Transfer-Encoding`. If we compress at runtime and an intermediate strips or re-chunks, that could corrupt framing.

Priya R: runtime shows repeated `504 upstream read timeout` followed by client reconnects. Access logs show occasional `502 Bad Gateway` and `499 Client Closed Request` spikes when they open 6 concurrent streams.

Jordan M: concurrent streams + idle keepalive might trigger connection pool pressure; an overloaded worker may close socket mid-event. Two immediate mitigations: 1) Ask Orchard to reduce concurrency during demo (e.g., 2 streams), 2) apply a short-lived account-level disable for stream concurrency enforcement (Samira-style exception).

Noah B: for a quick demo workaround, ask client to use a streaming-safe decoder snippet (browser JS): ```const reader = resp.body.getReader(); const dec = new TextDecoder(); let acc=''; async function pump(){ for(;;){ const {done, value} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; acc += dec.decode(value, {stream:true}); while(acc.includes("\n\n")){ const idx = acc.indexOf("\n\n"); const evt = acc.slice(0, idx); acc = acc.slice(idx+2); // handle SSE parse of evt lines
  // join data: lines into one payload
  const payload = evt.split(/\r?\n/).filter(l=>l.startsWith('data:')).map(l=>l.slice(5)).join(''); try{ const obj = JSON.parse(payload); /* handle */ }catch(e){ /* wait for more */ }
 }
 }
} pump();```

Priya R: I'll push that snippet to Orchard as a stopgap. They prefer not to change client if possible. They asked whether this is specific to Hosted (api.redwood) or also affects Dedicated/Private.

Jordan M: this is an edge of our flushing behavior in the serving runtime. It can surface in Hosted and Dedicated if the same flush policy (chunked/text) is used. Private on-prem might vary by customer proxy settings. We'll prioritize a fix but need customer-facing rollback plan.

Noah B: immediate small server-side mitigations we can try: - disable gzip for event-stream responses (set `Content-Encoding: identity`), - ensure `res.write('\n\n')` only after a full event is emitted, - on nginx we can add `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;`. Also setting `Cache-Control: no-transform` prevents intermediate proxies from altering streaming payloads.

Priya R: can we flip gzip off for Orchard org id for the demo as a temporary feature-flag?

Jordan M: yes. I'll create a feature-flag toggle and flip `streaming.disable_compression` for their org for 24 hours. That should reduce corruption from intermediate layers doing eager re-chunking.

SupportBot: Created task RED-INF-4823: "streaming: avoid splitting multi-byte chars on flush + org-level compression toggle" assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P1.

Noah B: engineering follow-up: we'll add defensive write that ensures we only flush at event boundaries and use a UTF-8 aware chunker. Quick patch can be behind a flag and enabled for Hosted orgs. Timeline estimate: 72 hours for safe roll, 1 week for full test matrix (Dedicated/Private).

Priya R: for demo today I'll: 1) share client decoder snippet, 2) reduce their concurrency to 2 streams, 3) flip the compression flag once Jordan confirms, and 4) ask them to run a small curl verification: ```curl -H "Accept:text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?sid=orx-poc-20260324-a1" --raw > raw.out && hexdump -C raw.out | sed -n '1,120p'```

Jordan M: will flip flag and post back when done. Also attaching a short nginx snippet to our presales playbook: ```location /v1/stream { proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no; }```

Noah B: adding to support checklist: 1) ask for raw hexdump, 2) check Content-Encoding & Transfer-Encoding headers, 3) grep runtime logs for request_id, 4) throttle concurrency for repro, 5) toggle compression flag as stopgap, 6) prioritize runtime fix ticket.

Priya R: demo update: after applying client snippet + reduce concurrency they still saw occasional parse warnings but no crash. Jordan: please confirm when flag is on so we can fully validate.

Jordan M: feature-flag on for org orchardrx (temp). Please re-run the curl and paste raw hexdump.

Priya R: curl hexdump attached to ticket RED-INF-4823. Looks much cleaner now, no mid-surrogate splits. Orchard passed their internal tests and demo went well. They want a permanent fix before production.

Noah B: follow-up plan: move the runtime patch to P0 for this quarter, include Dedicated validation, and update presales docs with the nginx + client snippets. Closing thread once ticket has ETA and PRs linked.

Priya R: thanks team. I'll close with Orchard and keep them updated on RED-INF-4823. :white_check_mark:
